key_insight: Positional disorder in realistic resonant dipole-dipole interacting networks can strongly localize quantum excitations, even though the coupling is partially long-ranged and radiative.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a route to robust control of exciton transport and trapping for coherent photovoltaics, excitonic devices, quantum memory, and quantum sensing.
method: Model spin/atom networks with realistic resonant dipole-dipole interaction (RDDI).
Introduce positional disorder and analyze coherent plus dissipative coupling effects.
Compare excitation dynamics across wavelengths to identify extended-to-localized behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a wavelength-induced transition from extended to localized excitation dynamics, supported by analysis of localized modes in disordered RDDI networks.
watch_item: Because RDDI is dissipative and not a simple power-law interaction, translating these localization effects into practical devices may require careful control of geometry, disorder, and loss.
paper_title: Quantum state localization in dipole-dipole interacting disordered networks
